who: The Foolish Old Man · Liezi ch. 5, tr. Lionel Giles, 1912
quote: Though I myself must die, I shall leave a son behind me... the mountain will receive no increment or addition. Why then should I despair of levelling it to the ground at last?
meaning: Almost 90, he moved a mountain one basket at a time. The mountain cannot grow. His work can go on.

who: The Buddha · Anguttara Nikaya 3.92, tr. Bhikkhu Sujato
quote: That farmer has no special power or ability to say: 'Let the crops germinate today!' ... But there comes a time when that farmer's crops germinate, flower, and ripen as the seasons change.
meaning: No farmer can make seeds grow today. Keep working, and they grow in their own time.

who: Tiruvalluvar · Tirukkural 620, tr. G. U. Pope, 1886
quote: Who strive with undismayed, unfaltering mind, / At length shall leave opposing fate behind.
meaning: Keep trying. One day, bad luck is left behind you.

who: Yang Sa-eon · Korean sijo poem, 16th century
quote: Soaring high though a mountain may be, it is a mere mound beneath Heaven / Climb and climb, and no summit cannot be reached / Yet people stay at its base saying the mountain is too high.
meaning: No mountain is too high to climb. The people who say 'too high' just stay at the bottom.

who: Confucius · Analects II.4, tr. James Legge
quote: At fifteen, I had my mind bent on learning. At thirty, I stood firm... At seventy, I could follow what my heart desired, without transgressing what was right.
meaning: Confucius kept growing from 15 to 70. Learning has no finish line.

who: The Buddha · Dhammapada 81, tr. F. Max Müller, 1881
quote: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
meaning: If people laugh at your practice, be a rock in the wind. Keep going.

who: R. Sharath Jois · Foreword to Yoga Mala, 2009
quote: Guruji created a strong foundation of yoga for us by teaching with such dedication for so many years. It is our duty to build upon that foundation... from him we should learn, be inspired, and carry on.
meaning: Our teachers built the base over many years. Our job is to keep building on it.

who: Vannupatha Jataka, No. 2 · tr. Robert Chalmers, 1895
quote: Untiring, deep they dug that sandy track / Till, in the trodden way, they water found. / So let the sage, in perseverance strong, / Flag not nor tire, until his heart find Peace.
meaning: In the desert, they kept digging in the same place until they found water. Do not stop digging.

who: Krishna · Bhagavad Gita 6.40, tr. Edwin Arnold, 1885
quote: He is not lost, thou Son of Pritha! No! / Nor earth, nor heaven is forfeit, even for him, / Because no heart that holds one right desire / Treadeth the road of loss!
meaning: No good effort is ever wasted. Every morning on the mat still counts.

who: Swami Vivekananda · The Real Nature of Man, London lecture
quote: Know the Truth and practice the Truth. The goal may be distant, but awake, arise, and stop not till the goal is reached.
meaning: The goal may be far away. Wake up, get up, and do not stop until you get there.
